scope_note: Second-pass public-evidence audit for the individual 654,433-square-foot IM3-mapped building footprint within Meta's Los Lunas data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW. The review covered the original campus chronology and 2016 industrial-revenue-bond package; Village budgets, audits, LEDA and dedicated infrastructure funds, planning, building, traffic, fire and water records; Valencia County assessor and clerk access; New Mexico economic-development, workforce, Construction Industries Division, Public Regulation Commission and Environment Department materials; PNM regulatory filings; Meta operator, SEC, contractor, career and grant materials; recipient-reported community records; and federal environmental and county-outcome access through September 6, 2026. Fifteen new direct observations are added alongside the two retained baseline observations, all at unallocated campus, company-county or supporting-infrastructure scope because no public source crosswalks the selected IM3 footprint to a separately named building, permit, parcel, workforce, utility meter or fiscal account. The later 2021 two-building expansion, 2023 three-building expansion load, 2025 AI expansion, off-site renewable projects, tenant equipment and other Meta facilities are excluded. No synthesis fragment is added because the selected building's operating date is not identified and the original six-building construction and operating sequence cannot support an isolated county treatment. Building-level capital expenditure, permits and fees, payroll, resident employment, supplier payments, metered electricity and water, utility bills, tax or PILOT payments, cash value of realized abatements, public-service costs and net fiscal results remain unobserved.

project_updates.title: Boundary and operating chronology verified
project_updates.notes: IM3 record 00626785488 is one 654,433-square-foot mapped footprint within a multi-building Los Lunas campus and supplies no building name or public-record crosswalk. State and Village records date the first campus groundbreaking to October 2016, the first online building to 2017, a campus grand opening to February 7, 2019, and six online buildings to 2022. They do not identify which chronology belongs to the selected footprint. The later 2021 two-building expansion, the three-building expansion load described in 2023, the 2025 AI expansion, tenant equipment, off-site renewable projects and other Meta facilities remain outside the selected-building boundary.
project_updates.project_description: Meta Los Lunas is a Meta-operated data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW in the Village of Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico; the selected project is the individual IM3-mapped 654,433-square-foot building footprint, not the full campus. State and Village records show the campus broke ground in October 2016, its first building was online in 2017, and Meta held a campus grand opening on February 7, 2019 while an original six-building program was still being built. The boundary excludes the separately announced 2021 two-building expansion, the 2025 AI expansion, off-site renewable projects, tenant equipment, and other Meta facilities.

project_updates.title: Original incentive authorization is not realized value
project_updates.notes: The June 23, 2016 bond package and Ordinance 407 were reviewed for original-project terms. Authorization for as many as six $5 billion industrial-revenue-bond series is a financing ceiling, not issued principal, capital expenditure, tax abatement, cash grant, property-tax saving or public cost. Later 2021 and 2025 bond packages concern expansions and are excluded. No selected-building bond draw, lease payment or realized incentive value was located.

project_updates.title: Campus parcel is fully exempt in the 2023 assessor revision
project_updates.notes: The exact address resolves to Village-owned UPC 1006040261023 / account R302913, a 738.15-acre campus parcel with business name FACEBOOK. The 2023 County fields report $19,930,050 actual value, $6,643,350 total assessed value, an equal other exemption and zero net assessed value. Those stocks are retained at unallocated campus scope; they are not a cash estimate of tax savings. Village FY2017-FY2023 GASB 77 schedules separately mark the Greater Kudu agreement under construction and PILOT receipts N/A for the school district, State and County. The report's unrelated $450,000 Village-wide PILOT total is excluded, and no selected-building or personal-property account, bill, payment, taxing-jurisdiction receipt, lease revenue, service cost or net fiscal result was found.

project_updates.title: Public-cost search supports fund flows with scope limits
project_updates.notes: Village budgets from FY2017 through FY2025, Resolution 16-26, the 2021 PPA amendment and dedicated infrastructure accounts were searched for State LEDA, Local LEDA GRT, Facebook, Greater Kudu and Meta flows. The original formula dedicated 75% of specified Village gross-receipts-tax distributions attributable to construction. Actual State LEDA receipts total $10 million across FY2017-FY2018; FY2021 actual outlays are $2,043,636 in the State project fund and $1,130,805 in the local fund. The FY2024 NM 6 traffic account separately reports $529,277 of revenue and $23,200 of capital purchases, and Village records identify Meta as payer for the completed off-site system. Receipts and expenditures are separate flows and are not summed or netted. The 2021 amendment says Greater Kudu declined some reimbursements and the Village would contract directly for revised infrastructure, but gives no dollar reconciliation. None of these funds is an IM3-building allocation or a complete marginal public-cost account.

project_updates.title: Permit, planning, construction and fire searches lack an IM3 crosswalk
project_updates.notes: The Village planning and zoning agenda archive, development-plan and permit page, fire-prevention and public-works access points, and state Construction Industries Division portal were searched for 2016-2026. The exact campus address returned 20 state records: 11 electrical, five mechanical, three general-construction and one modular record, with 13 closed and seven issued statuses. Their 2021-2026 labels use VCN, VLL6, later halls, administrative or temporary work; one detail page records a passed 2024 security final inspection, but no record supplies an IM3 crosswalk, permit fee or certificate of occupancy. No selected-building permit valuation, fee, inspection, construction start or contractor-payment value can be established, and post-2020 work is not used as original-building evidence. Complete applications, approved plans, fee receipts, inspection histories and certificates remain records-request targets for CID and the Village.

project_updates.title: Water agreement supplies capacity, not use
project_updates.notes: The original and restated agreement recitals, the August 2021 water-connection agreement, Village project-status and budget records, state water-right access and public water-planning materials were reviewed. The original 303-acre property received up to 500 acre-feet per year of consumptive water rights, converted to 0.446371233 million gallons per day for the direct record. A later Tank 7 connection was budgeted at $995,000 and Greater Kudu agreed to pay all design, construction and observation costs, but neither item is a realized payment and both remain unallocated campus infrastructure. The agreement's 4.5-million-gallon worst-case delivery guarantee and 1.5-million-gallon wastewater ceiling are capacities, not use; the reported 153,000-gallon 2020 campus average could not be tied to a public meter record. Village meter histories, bills, reimbursement ledgers, connection invoices and OSE diversion records remain request targets.

project_updates.title: Electric utility and regulatory searches isolate no building account
project_updates.notes: PNM and NMPRC materials for the original special-service contract and cases 16-00191-UT, 18-00269-UT, 21-00031-UT, 23-00251-UT and 25-00048-UT were reviewed. The 2018 notice confirms Greater Kudu's contribution-to-production mechanism, Meta's payment guaranty and customer recovery of specified renewable PPA costs, but supplies no realized dollar amount. Public versions do not disclose an IM3-building utility identity, meter, demand, consumption, bill, payment, customer contribution in aid of construction or original-campus interconnection outlay. PNM meter histories, billing determinants, invoices, receipts and interconnection work orders remain request targets; off-site or expansion-linked renewable-project spending, landowner payments and jobs are excluded.

project_updates.title: Environmental permit is site-wide and non-operational
project_updates.notes: New Mexico Environment Department air applications, permit notices, facility and emissions registries, compliance histories and feasibility materials were searched for Greater Kudu, Meta, 4250 Messenger Loop, agency interest 37303 and permit 7026 from 2016-2026. The 2024 application carries forward 118 permitted stationary generators plus two temporary units for the full source and distinguishes VLL from later VCN groups, but the public copy omits the referenced plot-plan appendix and supplies no IM3 crosswalk. Compliance tables list NOx, CO and opacity test dates from 2019-2023 without results; the state EPA-reporting layer returns no exact-name or exact-address record. The permitted count is retained as a site-wide stock, while potential emissions, ratings and tests do not prove runtime, diesel use, actual emissions, electric load, water use or environmental damages. NMED inspection reports, test results, annual emissions, excess-emission reports, tank and stormwater files remain request targets.

project_updates.title: Operator, SEC and workforce sources retain payroll gaps
project_updates.notes: Meta's 2019 opening release, current Los Lunas materials, 2021 expansion release, 2025 Form 10-K, New Mexico economic-development and Workforce Solutions reports, BLS OEWS access and current job postings were searched for headcount, occupation, wage, payroll, residence and hiring evidence. The opening release supports more than 150 campus jobs, while a 2018 state review repeats forecasts of 800-1,000 daily construction workers through 2023 and about 300 permanent jobs at full six-building operation; forecasts are not actuals. No source identifies filled selected-building headcount, direct versus contractor status, FTEs, wages, benefits, worker residence, occupations or hiring dates. Current 400-plus job and $2.5-billion campus figures include or anticipate later expansion and are excluded; statewide or Albuquerque-area occupation wages are not substituted for Meta payroll.

project_updates.title: Supplier and procurement searches produce identities, not payments
project_updates.notes: State economic-development reports, Village budgets, operator releases, CID permits and searches for Fortis, APIC Solutions, Southland Industries, Cache Valley Electric, B&D Industries and other named contractors were reviewed. The records identify contractors, equipment providers and construction activity but disclose no contract value, invoice, payment date, local purchasing share, supplier payroll or selected-building allocation. The separate $37 million PNM solar contract and renewable-project construction statistics concern off-site generation, not Los Lunas data-center supplier spending, and are excluded.

project_updates.title: Community and recipient records support non-additive grants
project_updates.notes: Village newsletters and agendas, Meta grant materials, the 2023 PNM filing appendix and recipient reports from Explora and named schools and nonprofits were reviewed for 2017-2026. Direct observations retain Meta's greater-than-$3.1-million cumulative Valencia County funding through June 2023, the $225,000 Wi-Fi grant and the $212,000 arithmetic sum of 17 May 2023 awards. These company-county figures overlap and must not be summed or assigned to the selected building. Meta's November 2025 program update reports more than 210 Los Lunas-area grants and sponsorships since 2019 but no local dollar total; a May 2026 Village quorum notice confirms another ceremony without amounts. Recipient sources generally confirmed relationships but did not disclose additional exact amounts, payment dates, restricted balances or building attribution.

project_updates.title: County outcomes and residual modeling remain unsupported
project_updates.notes: The direct-evidence audit ends with no residual model because no public record identifies when IM3 footprint 00626785488 opened or separates its construction and operations from the five other original campus buildings. The first building was online in 2017, the campus opened publicly in 2019, and six buildings were online by 2022, creating staggered treatment alongside other Valencia County developments and later Meta expansion. BLS QCEW county and industry files, BEA county accounts and Census workforce access were checked as potential comparison series, but they cannot identify the selected building, direct versus contractor employment, worker residence or a defensible treatment date; simultaneous county development and disclosure suppression add further limits. Without building-level capital, employment, payroll, supplier, utility and fiscal anchors, a county difference, multiplier, avoided-cost or residual estimate would manufacture precision. No synthesis fragment is created.
